title: Partitioning a support fiber by the symbol at one coordinate
statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite alphabet, and let $u$ be a word of length $n$ over $\alpha$, that is, a function $u \colon \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \alpha$. Fix a set $S \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}\,n$ of coordinate positions together with a further position $i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,n$, and let $F$ be the support fiber of $u$ over $\{i\} \cup S$, namely the set of words that differ from $u$ in exactly the positions belonging to $\{i\} \cup S$. Since $i$ lies in $\{i\} \cup S$, every word in $F$ carries at position $i$ some symbol distinct from $u_i$, and grouping the words of $F$ by that symbol partitions $F$: it equals the disjoint union, taken over all symbols $a \in \alpha$ with $a \ne u_i$, of the sets $\{v \in F : v_i = a\}$,
\[
  F = \bigsqcup_{\substack{a \in \alpha \\ a \ne u_i}} \{\, v \in F : v_i = a \,\}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: a word u of length n over α
a set S of coordinate positions
replaced:
For a word $u$, a set $S$ of positions, and a position $i$, the support fiber over
$\{i\} \cup S$ is partitioned by the value chosen at position $i$:
\[
  \mathrm{supportFiber}(u, \{i\} \cup S)
  = \bigsqcup_{a \in \mathrm{choices}(u,i)}
    \{v \in \mathrm{supportFiber}(u,\{i\}\cup S) : v_i = a\}.
\]
